headline: An expired 2013 Secure Boot certificate anchors a broad open-source patching day, as Debian ships its sixth trixie update, AI surfaces a 15-year-old Linux root flaw, and RedHook Android malware turns wireless debugging into a shell.

emerging_trends.text: Trust infrastructure baked into hardware a decade ago is reaching end of life, and the expired 2013 Secure Boot certificate that signs bootloaders on most PCs now forces mass firmware updates.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Expired Secure Boot Certificate Forces Firmware Updates

emerging_trends.text: AI has crossed from attack surface to bug hunter, with an AI system surfacing a Linux root flaw that reviewers overlooked for 15 years.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Uncovers a 15-Year-Old Linux Root Flaw

emerging_trends.text: Mobile banking malware keeps repurposing legitimate Android tooling, and RedHook now abuses Wireless ADB to grab shell privileges with no computer attached.
emerging_trends.topic_title: RedHook Android Malware Abuses Wireless ADB

topics.title: Expired Secure Boot Certificate Forces Firmware Updates
topics.latest_developments: Debian released 13.6 'trixie' on July 12, 2026, bundling more than a hundred security advisories and routing a fix for the now-expired 2013 UEFI Secure Boot certificate through an updated fwupd.
topics.summary: Most PCs ship a UEFI Secure Boot certificate authority installed by default since 2013 that signs the bootloaders letting machines start with Secure Boot on; that certificate has expired, and Debian's point release patches the trust chain via fwupd. Administrators running Debian 13 should apply 13.6 and update firmware to keep Secure Boot functioning.

sources.title: Debian 13.6 security update patches over a hundred advisories in trixie

topics.title: RedHook Android Malware Abuses Wireless ADB
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported July 12, 2026 that a new RedHook variant abuses Android Wireless Debugging, or Wireless ADB, to gain shell-level privileges on a phone without any computer connection.
topics.summary: RedHook is Android malware that now escalates to shell access by turning on the operating system's own wireless debugging feature, a technique that sidesteps the usual requirement for a tethered computer. Android users should disable Wireless Debugging, avoid sideloaded apps, and watch for unexpected developer-mode prompts.

sources.title: RedHook Android malware now uses Wireless ADB for shell access

topics.title: Wireshark 4.6.7 Patches a Dozen Flaws
topics.latest_developments: The SANS Internet Storm Center noted July 11, 2026 that Wireshark 4.6.7 fixes 12 vulnerabilities and 16 bugs in the widely used network protocol analyzer.
topics.summary: Wireshark, the packet-capture and protocol-analysis tool that security teams run daily, shipped a maintenance release closing a dozen security flaws. Analysts should upgrade to 4.6.7, since malformed captures can trigger dissector vulnerabilities.

topics.title: AI Uncovers a 15-Year-Old Linux Root Flaw
topics.latest_developments: Wired reported July 11, 2026 that an AI system found a root-privilege bug in Linux that human reviewers had missed for 15 years, alongside word that the Pentagon is training amateurs into a hacker corps and that a Flock license-plate-reader error led police to surround a car reviewer.
topics.summary: An AI tool identified a long-buried root-level vulnerability in the Linux kernel, underscoring how machine analysis now finds flaws that eluded a decade and a half of human eyes. Linux operators should track the disclosure and patch once a fix lands.

sources.title: AI Found a Root Bug in Linux That Everyone Missed for 15 Years

business_politics.title: U.S. and Iran Trade New Strikes Over Hormuz
business_politics.latest_developments: The United States launched multiple fresh waves of strikes on Iranian military targets Sunday, July 12, and Iranian forces fired on commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, sending oil prices higher as the ceasefire collapsed further.
business_politics.summary: Iran insists it has closed the Strait of Hormuz, the chokepoint for roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, while President Trump says the waterway stays open; the escalating tit-for-tat strikes threaten crude flows and revive inflation fears that could keep the Federal Reserve on hold.

business.title: Pennsylvania Enacts $50.8 Billion Budget
business.latest_developments: Governor Josh Shapiro signed a $50.8 billion state budget into law Sunday, July 12, twelve days past the statutory deadline, after the Pennsylvania Senate gave its approval.
business.summary: The fifth consecutive overdue Pennsylvania budget steers additional aid to the commonwealth's poorest school districts and skips difficult policy fights; last year's impasse dragged into November.

sources.title: Gov. Josh Shapiro signs $50.8 billion state budget into law

around_town.title: Another Heat Wave Hits Midweek
around_town.latest_developments: A strong heat dome centered over the Midwest will slide into Western Pennsylvania by midweek, driving highs into the 90s from Tuesday, July 14, through at least Thursday, July 16.
around_town.summary: Meteorologists at WPXI expect the Midwest heat dome to nudge east over the Pittsburgh area, returning 90-degree temperatures for several days after a milder stretch.
